correctness.rationale: Fix an image set S of size r. Every surjection onto S is equally likely, and each fixed point is in S. For k prescribed indices in S, fixing those k outputs leaves an inclusion–exclusion count of completions that hit the other r−k labels. Summing over the (r)_k ordered choices yields exactly the displayed moment; the same count is the probability of distinct initial k outputs of a uniform surjection. This proves mean one (k=1), and Var(F)=a₂, with r=1 giving F=1. For iid uniform outputs D counts distinct first-k labels. The probability of full coverage given D=d is nondecreasing in d by inclusion of the sets that still must be hit. Conditioning on coverage thus increases the probability of the top event D=k, proving the lower moment bound, while the distinctness interpretation gives a_k≤1. Expanding the PGF at 1 gives the stated sandwich for z≥1. The birthday bound 1−a_k≤binom(k,2)/r extends to k>r because then the right side is at least one. Factorial inversion is finite for F and absolutely convergent for Poisson(1); summing absolute differences gives (1/2)Σ 2^k(1−a_k)/k!≤e²/r. This includes r=n and is uniform in n. For fixed r the iid output list is onto with probability at least 1−r(1−1/r)^n, so the moments converge to the binomial moments on the same finite support, implying TV convergence. The frozen checker was inspected, not run; its recorded finite tests are not evidence for the uniform estimate or either limit.

value.rationale: Image rank is a natural coarse observable distinct from a fixed occupancy profile or the set of cyclic vertices. The moment comparison gives a uniform finite control of the change caused by conditioning only on rank and explains why even very sparse growing ranks have Poisson fixed-point counts, whereas bounded ranks give a different binomial regime. The finite-rank rate requires no relative scaling of n, and the lower moment and variance comparisons give information not contained in the exact mean or qualitative profile criterion.
